text:
Similar business development will dominate the south side of Lincoln Highway in the Village of Matteson from the Illinois Central Railroad tracks west to Cicero Avenue, except for the cemetery land and the residential area immediately to the east of it.
Thus, the improvement on Lincoln Highway will not change the character of the developed areas surrounding it and should improve the neighborhoods through which it passes by providing quicker, smoother and safer east-west travel to both Interstate Route 57 and the Calumet Expressway, to the park-and-ride station at the Illinois Central Railroad crossing and for inter-neighborhood and shopping-oriented travel.
Alternate "B" was laid out in an attempt to minimize the disruption to existing land use by shifting the centerline for the improvement away from the built-up side of the existing roadway in those areas where one side of the right-of-way was open and undeveloped. During the course of the study, however, subdivisions were created and development took place that mitigated the opportunities sought by this alignment.
Alternate "A" was designed to place the proposed new centerline generally along the existing centerline, and therefore, necessitates comparable takings along both sides of the existing roadway. These required takings, however, are approximately one-half as wide as those that would be needed under the concept of Alternate "B". Alternate "A", therefore diminishes the width of takings to a point which permits, in most cases, the existing development along the roadway to continue in use.
As the study progressed, Alternate "B" was dropped on the basis that it was no longer a feasible and prudent alternate due to the probable significant adverse disruption of land development that had occurred along the route. Alternate "A" was the only one presented at the public hearing.
It is the recommendation of the Illinois Department of Transportation that Lincoln Highway be reconstructed between Cicero Avenue and Chicago Road on the alternate alignment "A" discussed and described above.
